sections.html:
Centerton is a city in Benton County, about 5 miles west of Bentonville on Arkansas Highway 102, which is the main road through the middle of town. Bentonville is the county seat and sits about 5 miles east, so commute time to Bentonville is the first thing many buyers ask about. Northwest Arkansas Regional Airport lies south of the city.

The city grew quickly. It had 2,146 residents in 2000 and 17,792 in 2020, and the 2025 estimate is 27,176. The 2020 census counted 6,280 housing units, with 5.6% of them vacant. Because Centerton is largely a suburb of Bentonville, many buyers arrive through the regional job base, which includes Walmart, Tyson Foods and J.B. Hunt, or through relocations.

Centerton is one of the fastest-growing cities in Arkansas, and the housing stock has grown with it. A seller with an older house now competes with a lot of newer construction nearby, which is why condition and price matter so much.

sections.h2: Schools and why buyers ask about them
sections.html: Most of Centerton is in the Bentonville School District, and a very small western portion is in the Decatur School District. Bentonville West High School is located in Centerton. Centerton Gamble Elementary serves much of the city, though other areas are zoned to different elementary schools. Zoning differs by street, so confirm the school assignment for your address before you share it with a buyer.

Centerton's Building Safety department issues building, plumbing, electrical, mechanical, demolition, pool and solar permits, and it reviews plans. Inspections are scheduled through an online portal at bsaonline.com. Fire inspections are handled separately by the Fire Marshal or Fire Chief. A certificate of occupancy is issued before a structure is occupied, which mostly matters for new or newly finished construction.

You can email buildingsafety@centertonar.us or call 479-795-2750 to ask about older work or open permits.

Before you list, check these items:

  • Whether a deck, shed, pool or addition has a permit on file.
  • Whether any open permit still needs a final inspection.
  • Whether your subdivision has covenants that limit changes.

A buyer's lender or inspector will find an unpermitted addition, and it can stall a closing. Sorting it out early gives you more choices.

Benton County sits on the Springfield Plateau, a karst area of springs, sinkholes and caves. Centerton itself grew up around a spring, so drainage, runoff and ground conditions around a house are fair questions from a buyer. Roof condition after storms and the heating system after cold snaps come up too. Know the answers before the first showing.

sections.h2: Property tax due dates and penalties
sections.html:
The Benton County collector bills the tax. The books open on the first business day of March, and a 10 percent penalty applies to anything unpaid after October 15. Real estate that stays unpaid also accrues interest. Tax statements must be mailed by July 1.

Taxes are paid one year behind, so a 2026 assessment is billed in 2027 and due October 15, 2027. The bill goes to the owner of record on January 1 of the tax year. Closing documents explain how the buyer and seller split it. If a mortgage company receives the bill, check within 30 to 60 days that it was paid.

sections.h2: How a sale changes your assessment
sections.html:
The Benton County assessor appraises a sold house at 20 percent of appraised value at the next assessment date after title transfers. A new owner cannot claim an assessed-value limitation until the second assessment date after transfer. The homestead credit is up to $600 for a primary residence. The county's next reappraisal is 2028.

Arkansas also charges a transfer tax of $3.30 per $1,000 of consideration on transfers above $100. The state's transfer tax page has the details.

sections.h2: What do Centerton sellers usually face?
sections.html:
Sellers here often have a newer house in a busy area, a relocation, an inherited property, or a rental. Some have a house that needs repairs a conventional buyer's lender would require.

A cash offer removes the lender's appraisal and repair requirements, so the sale does not hinge on a buyer's loan approval. Compare it with a listing on timing and on what you would net, and ask for the offer in writing. Before you agree to anything, gather your tax statement, any permit paperwork and your mortgage payoff information so you can compare offers on equal terms.

faqs.a: Centerton is in Benton County, about 5 miles west of Bentonville on Arkansas Highway 102. Decatur is 11 miles farther west.

faqs.q: What school district is Centerton in?
faqs.a: Most of Centerton is in the Bentonville School District, and a small western part is in the Decatur School District. Bentonville West High School is in Centerton.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Centerton?
faqs.a: October 15 is the deadline, with a 10 percent penalty after it. The Benton County collector opens the books on the first business day of March.

faqs.q: Do I need a certificate of occupancy to sell my Centerton house?
faqs.a: A certificate of occupancy is issued before a structure is occupied, so it applies to new or newly finished construction. Call Building Safety at 479-795-2750 about older work or open permits.

faqs.q: Does the sale change my assessment?
faqs.a: Yes. The Benton County assessor reappraises a sold house at 20 percent of appraised value at the next assessment date after title transfers.
